headline: World is 27% of the way to protecting a third of Earth
meta_description: Nearly every country has committed to conserving 30% of land and sea by 2030. New research shows 27% may already be protected.
summary_short: Almost every country has agreed to protect 30% of the world's land and sea by 2030—and we may already be closer than we think.
body:
Almost every country has agreed to conserve 30% of the world's land and sea by 2030. A new study reveals that 27% of land may already be conserved for biodiversity—suggesting the goal is within striking distance.

This near-universal commitment represents a rare moment of global consensus on environmental protection. The agreement signals that nations across every continent recognize the urgency of preserving ecosystems before it's too late.

The fact that existing conservation efforts may already cover more than four-fifths of the target is encouraging. It means the remaining work, while significant, builds on foundations already in place rather than starting from scratch. Whether through protected areas, indigenous land stewardship, or restoration projects, the world is demonstrating that large-scale biodiversity protection is achievable.
quick_facts: 30% land and sea protection target by 2030
Almost every country has committed to the goal
27% of land may already be conserved for biodiversity
